nodes.summary: The complement of a decreasing event is increasing (`IsLowerSet.compl`).
nodes.title: Complement of a decreasing event is increasing

nodes.summary: The complement of an increasing event is decreasing (`IsUpperSet.compl`).
nodes.title: Complement of an increasing event is decreasing

nodes.summary: The *FKG lattice condition* on a weight `π : ConfigSpace E → ℝ`: `π ω * π ω' ≤ π (ω ⊔ ω') * π (ω ⊓ ω')` for all configurations `ω ω'`. For a positive weight this is log-supermodularity. Mathlib's `fkg` and `holley` state it in the form `π a * π b ≤ π (a ⊓ b) * π (a ⊔ b)`.
nodes.title: FKG lattice condition

nodes.summary: The real indicator function of an increasing event is monotone.
nodes.title: Indicator of an increasing event is monotone

nodes.summary: The intersection of two increasing events is increasing (`IsUpperSet.inter`).
nodes.title: Intersection of two increasing events is increasing

nodes.summary: An event `A ⊆ ConfigSpace E` is *decreasing* if it is a lower set for the coordinatewise order. This is `IsLowerSet A`.
nodes.title: Decreasing event

nodes.summary: An intersection of increasing events is increasing (`isUpperSet_iInter`).
nodes.title: Arbitrary intersections of increasing events are increasing

nodes.summary: An event is increasing iff its real indicator function is monotone. See also `Set.monotone_mem`, the analogous statement for the `Prop`-valued membership predicate.
nodes.title: An event is increasing iff its indicator is monotone

nodes.summary: An event `A ⊆ ConfigSpace E` is *increasing* if it is an upper set for the coordinatewise order: `ω ∈ A` and `ω ≤ ω'` imply `ω' ∈ A`. This is `IsUpperSet A`.
nodes.title: Increasing event

nodes.summary: A log-modular weight, `π ω * π ω' = π (ω ⊔ ω') * π (ω ⊓ ω')`, satisfies the FKG lattice condition.
nodes.title: Log-modular weights satisfy the FKG lattice condition

nodes.summary: The union of two increasing events is increasing (`IsUpperSet.union`).
nodes.title: Union of two increasing events is increasing

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
